\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Contraction}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Randomization.Contraction
\section{Overview}
Coordinate noise admits a negative contraction rate depending only on its exponent. Positive and negative coordinate contractions combine into contraction for anisotropic noise with independent signs.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Negative coordinate-noise contraction for exponents at least two]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.coordinate_noise_negative_contraction}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.CenteredContraction.scalar_contraction, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.laplacian, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.condExp_negative_moment_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.coordinateNoise}
\difficulty{4}
For every $q\in\mathbb R$ with $q\ge2$, there exists $c\in\mathbb R$ with $0<c\le1$, and
with $c=2/5$ whenever $q=4$, such that the following holds for every nonnegative integer
$n$, every product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive
coordinate atom weights summing to $1$, every coordinate $i$, and every real-valued
function $f$ on its outcome space: $\|N_{i,-c}f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{q,P}$. Here
$\|h\|_{q,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^q)^{1/q}$ and $N_{i,-c}h=h-L_i h-cL_i h$, with $L_i
h=h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Self-adjointness of coordinate noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.coordinateNoise_selfAdjoint}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp_selfAdjoint, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.laplacian, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.coordinateNoise}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a finite product of probability spaces whose coordinate atom weights are
strictly positive and sum to $1$, let $i$ be a coordinate, let $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and
let $f,g$ be real-valued functions on the product outcome space. If $N_{i,\rho}h=h-L_i
h+\rho L_i h$, where $L_i h=h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h$ and the conditional expectation
averages over coordinate $i$, then $\mathbb E_P[(N_{i,\rho}f)g]=\mathbb
E_P[f(N_{i,\rho}g)]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive coordinate noise contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.coordinate_noise_positive_contraction}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.laplacian, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.condExp_moment_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.weighted_abs_rpow_sum_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.coordinateNoise}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom
masses, let $i$ be a coordinate, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the product
space. For $0\leq\rho\leq1$ and $q\geq1$, the one-coordinate noise operator $N_{i,\rho}$
satisfies $\|N_{i,\rho}f\|_{q,P}\leq\|f\|_{q,P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Partial anisotropic noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.partialNoise}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $J\subseteq[n]$, rates $r_i\in\mathbb R$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Define $T_{J,\boldsymbol r}f(x)=\sum_S(\prod_{j\in S\cap J}r_j)f_S(x)$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Insertion of a Partial-Noise Coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.partialNoise_insert}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_sum_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.laplacian, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.condExp_component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.coordinateNoise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.partialNoise}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a finite product probability space with strictly positive coordinate weights,
let $J$ be a set of coordinates, let $r_i\in\mathbb R$ be rates, and let $f$ be a
real-valued function on the product space. For any coordinate $i\notin J$, applying
partial noise with coordinate set $J\cup\{i\}$ equals applying the one-coordinate noise
operator at $i$ with rate $r_i$ to the result of applying partial noise with coordinate
set $J$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Anisotropic noise contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.anisotropicNoise_norm_le_of_coordinate}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.component_reconstruction, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.anisotropicNoise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.coordinateNoise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.partialNoise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.partialNoise_insert}

Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom
masses, let $q\in\mathbb R$, let $r_i\in\mathbb R$ be a rate for each coordinate, and
let $T_{\boldsymbol r}$ denote the anisotropic noise operator and $N_{i,r_i}$ the noise
operator on coordinate $i$. If $\|N_{i,r_i}g\|_{q,P}\leq\|g\|_{q,P}$ for every
coordinate $i$ and every real-valued function $g$ on the product, then $\|T_{\boldsymbol

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Contraction under signed product noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.signed_anisotropicNoise_contraction}
